LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Sole possession of first place in the NFC North is on the line at Ford Field as two 8-2 rivals clash on Thanksgiving with long winning streaks Imagn Images In the first of three Thanksgiving day games, the Detroit Lions play host to the division rival Chicago Bears in one of the biggest games of the NFL season to date. Detroit enters this game winners of six straight and sitting in first place in the NFC North with an 8-2 record. The Lions sport one of the NFL's most efficient and explosive offenses, and their efense hasn't allowed more than 21 points in a game since all the way back in Week 4. The Lions are dealing with injury issues on that side of the ball, but they've held up surprisingly well. That will be put to the test on Thursday afternoon. Chicago comes into this game having won five in a row and sporting an 8-2 record that matches that of Detroit, with the Bears sitting in second place in the division by virtue of a tiebreaker. The Bears also have one of the league's best offenses, while the defense has been strengthened by the acquisition of superstar defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons , who seems to have transformed the unit up front and allowed everything else to click properly into place. That unit, too, will be tested more than ever here. Which of these two teams will keep its winning streak alive and lay claim to sole possession of first place in the division? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Lions vs. Bears live Date: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 1 p.m. ET Location: Ford Field (Detroit) TV: CBS | Streaming: Paramount+ Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -2.5, O/U 55.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bears have the ball Chicago is eighth in total yards and eighth in total points this season, but some of that has to do with volume. The Bears rank a surprising 14th in yards per play, 12th in points per drive and 15th in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. Some of that is due to the fact that Caleb Williams missed several games with a hamstring injury, but even with Williams on the field the Bears' EPA per play mark is only the equivalent of the 10th-best offense in the league. Chicago is one of the league's most run-oriented offenses, ranking ninth in the share of plays that turn into a rush attempt. But D'Andre Swift is averaging just 3.7 yards per carry and Kyle Monangai , who has been more effective (5.0 per carry) has played in only five games. The Lions have sported a top run defense this season in allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, but that defense took a couple of massive hits over the last few weeks with the losses of Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson to injury. Still, Detroit held Tampa Bay's running backs to 84 yards on 22 carries last Sunday, when Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell had previously been destroying teams on the ground. The Bears will need Swift and Monangai to find more success if they want to control the game in the fashion they have preferred since Ben Johnson became head coach last year. Chicago's passing game has been relatively inconsistent this year, as there have been times when Caleb Williams has looked like an elite quarterback and others when he has looked ordinary — sometimes within the same game. (Like the Sunday night showdown against the Buccaneers , for example.) Williams has completed 68.3% of his passes at 7.9 yards per attempt, but he's thrown only 10 touchdown passes against six interceptions. He's 11th in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, but he's been highly susceptible against the blitz: he ranks fourth in EPA against four-man rushes but only checks in 19th when opponents rush five or more. Detroit has blitzed at a below-average rate this season (30.3%, per Tru Media), but would be wise to turn up the pressure a bit against a quarterback who has shown that he can be pressured into some bad decisions on occasion if you get defenders into his lap. Still, the Lions have been highly susceptible to opposing passing attacks, even if they have been improved since the return of Brian Branch and should get another lift as Kerby Joseph rounds into form. The Lions are 27th in EPA per dropback allowed, and they're in the bottom third in opponents' explosive play rate through the air. Detroit is most vulnerable against opposing tight ends, allowing the league's fifth-highest target share to the position, so this could be a game where the Bears finally get Colston Loveland going in a way that they haven't been able to accomplish as much as they likely wanted to this year. The Lions do limit yards after the catch better than any defense in the NFL, though, allowing only 4.0 YAC per completion, according to Tru Media. That could take away from some of Chicago's success in the screen game and possibly limit the effectiveness of Luther Burden III and — to a lesser extent because he's not as big a part of the offense — Kalif Raymond . When the Lions have the ball The Lions are third in the NFL in yards and fifth in points. They're fifth in both yards per play and points per drive, as well as fifth in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. They're second in EPA per pass attempt and third in EPA per rush attempt. They're third in passing success rate, first in rushing success rate and third in overall success rate. They are, in other words, a top-five offense by almost any measurement, and they can beat you with both the pass and the run. Jared Goff is having a marvelous season, completing 67.8% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt with 20 touchdown passes against six interceptions. He's third in the league behind only Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow in EPA per dropback, third behind only Purdy and Burrow in success rate and fourth behind only Purdy, Burrow and Patrick Mahomes in passer rating. His 8.2 yards-per-attempt average is the second-best of his tenure in Detroit, as are the 52.3% success rate and 107.7 passer rating. He's of course blessed with one of the best skill-position corps in the league: Amon-Ra St. Brown is a picture of consistency; Jameson Williams is one of the most explosive threats in football; Sam LaPorta is a strong option and tight end; and Jahmyr Gibbs is the best running back in the NFL, leading the league in rushes, rushing yards, first downs, yards from scrimmage and total touchdowns. St. Brown often gets pigeonholed as a slot guy, but in reality he plays more outside (59.2% of snaps) than he does inside (39.8%), according to Tru Media, and he's equally capable of dominating defenses from either spot. He's Goff's first read more often than not because he runs a lot of short-area routes and the Lions like to get the ball out fairly quickly in their straight dropback game, where St. Brown is often the target. Williams is the guy the Lions turn toward when they're looking to test defenses in the intermediate and deep areas of the field. His 12.36-yard average route depth is fourth among 199 players who have run 100 or more routes this season, according to Tru Media, and he's generated an explosive gain (16-plus yards) on 26.3% of his targets, which ranks 17th among that same group of players. He and LaPorta are generally going to eat into each other's target shares in any given week, while St. Brown remains the more consistent top target. The Bears' secondary is beatable, as Chicago ranks 22nd in net yards allowed per attempt, according to Pro-Football-Reference. Jaylon Johnson is not the same player he once was, Tyrique Stevenson is inconsistent, Kyler Gordon has barely played and Malik Muhammad has the ups and downs of a fourth-round rookie. If the Lions give Goff time to throw, he could feast on this group all afternoon. That's where Chicago's improved defensive line comes in. Since acquiring Jeffery Simmons, the Bears rank seventh in the league in EPA per dropback, per Tru Media, in large part because they have recorded a sack on 10.7% of opponent dropbacks. Prior to acquiring Simmons, Chicago's sack rate was 8.9%. That figure still ranked third in the league through seven weeks, but it's been much improved since the Bears dropped Simmons into the middle of the defensive line. Detroit is pretty strong up front, allowing pressure on only 32.3% of dropbacks, which ranks sixth in the NFL. The sack rate is a bit worse than that because Goff isn't the world's most mobile quarterback, but he's generally given adequate time to throw. The Lions' run game is diverse, efficient and explosive. Gibbs is seventh in the NFL in yards per carry, fifth in the share of runs that gain five or more yards and second in explosive run rate, according to Tru Media. Detroit will battle with former offensive coordinator Ben Johnson and the 8-2 Chicago Bears in one of the most highly anticipated Turkey Day games in recent memory. With a victory, the Lions would not only capture a “statement win” but also improve to 3-0 against their NFC North opponents in 2026. Additionally, a win would provide Dan Campbell's squad with a significant leg-up in the race for the division crown. Detroit will be challenged every step of the way in the Week 12 clash. The Bears enter the holiday affair winners of five in a row, with both a top-10 offense (No. 8 in points per game) and a top-10 defense (No. 6 in points allowed/game). Plus, their defense received a major boost via the midseason trade for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Simmons, formerly of the Tennessee Titans, has already recorded nine sacks this season, and is coming off a three-sack performance in Week 11 against the New Orleans Saints. He's also generated 36 total pressures, and for his efforts, has earned Pro Football Focus’ fourth-highest pass-rush grade among 132 qualified interior defensive linemen (84.9). The two-time Pro Bowler is the definition of a difference-making defensive tackle. Consequently, it wouldn't be surprising to see the 6-foot-4, 305-pounder end up with a couple of pressures and possibly even a sack Thursday. Additional Lions NFL Insider Analysis: No Red Flags For Safety Kerby Joseph After 2026 Debut Then, on offense, the Bears are led by 25-year-old signal-caller Caleb Williams. The former No. 1 overall pick might not have the most prolific passing numbers (10 touchdowns and 1,727 yards in seven games), but he's still very much a force to be reckoned with (both with his right arm and his legs). For the season, he's completing a career-best 68.3 percent of his passes, and is throwing for a career-high 246.7 yards per game. And on top of that, he's posted a 68.9 QBR, the eighth-best mark among 30 qualified quarterbacks. Plus, he's a constant threat to pick up a first down with his legs, with 12 first downs on the ground this season. And although he hasn't made much of an impact as a runner in recent weeks, he still has 156 rushing yards and a couple of rushing scores to his name. Along with Williams, the Bears feature a pair of ultra talented wideouts : Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze. Burden leads all Chicago receivers in catches (51), reception yards (654) and receiving scores (four). Meanwhile, Odunze has also had a solid campaign, with 36 catches, 573 yards and a touchdown to his name. Burden and Odunze will likely be a handful for the Lions' injury-plagued cornerbacks group, which could be without No. 1 CB D.J. Reed (hip) for a fourth consecutive game. The Bears also possess a top-flight rushing attack, spearheaded by former Lions running back D'Andre Swift. Swift has compiled 627 yards and 10 touchdowns on 168 carries in 2026. And as a team, Chicago has amassed 1,424 yards on the ground, the third-most in the NFL through 11 weeks. Additionally, if I were a betting man, I'd put my money on Johnson dialing up a trick play or two against his former team. Simply, it will not be easy for Detroit to emerge victorious in this Week 12 affair. However, at this present juncture, I'll give the Lions a 52 percent chance to secure their seventh straight win . Adding fuel to the holiday fire, Chicago arrives in Detroit led by head coach Ben Johnson , the former Lions offensive coordinator making a high-stakes return to his old stomping grounds. While Chicago boasts an impressive 8-2 record, Detroit's explosive offense and home-field edge set the stage for a statement victory. Here are three bold predictions for Thursday's showdown. 1. Jahmyr Gibbs Eclipses 160 Total Yards and Two Touchdowns Jahmyr Gibbs has been an unstoppable force all season, already racking up 1,098 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns through 10 games. On a short week, explosive speed kills, and Detroit will lean heavily on its dynamic backfield weapon to dictate the tempo. While Chicago's defense has been opportunistic, the Bears enter Thursday banged up on the back end, defensive backs Kyler Gordon (shoulder) and Elijah Hicks (concussion) both missed practice early in the week. Look for Detroit to isolate Gibbs in space against Chicago's linebackers and depleted secondary. Whether slicing through the interior behind Detroit's physical front or turning routine checkdowns into chunk plays, Gibbs will clear 160 scrimmage yards and find the end zone twice, outdueling former Lion D'Andre Swift. 2. Jared Goff Shreds Chicago's Secondary for 325+ Yards and Zero Turnovers Ben Johnson knows Detroit's personnel inside and out, meaning the Bears will throw plenty of disguised coverages at Jared Goff. However, Goff has operated with surgical precision in 2026, throwing for 2,716 yards and 20 touchdowns against just four interceptions. With tight end Sam LaPorta trending toward playing after logging a full practice on Tuesday following an ankle issue, Goff will have his full arsenal available alongside Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. If Gordon and Hicks are sidelined or limited, Chicago simply lacks the perimeter depth to survive four quarters inside the fast track of Ford Field. Goff will pick apart zone windows, keep the ball completely out of harm's way, and top 325 passing yards in a clinical performance. 3. Detroit's Pass Rush Forces Caleb Williams into Three Second-Half Mistakes Chicago's offense has leaned heavily on its ground game and situational efficiency, as Caleb Williams enters Thursday with a modest 1,727 passing yards, 10 touchdowns, and six interceptions. Even if edge rusher DJ Wonnum (7 sacks) is limited or sidelined by a back injury, Detroit's defensive front ranks second in the NFL with 36 sacks, anchored by Alim McNeill. Once Detroit's fourth-ranked scoring offense builds a two-score lead in the second half, Chicago will be forced to abandon its balanced script and drop Williams back repeatedly against a roaring Ford Field crowd. Under relentless pressure, Williams will force throws into tight coverage, resulting in two interceptions and a strip-sack that slam the door on a Bears comeback. Ben Johnson's return brings undeniable intrigue, and Chicago's 8-2 mark proves the Bears are legitimate contenders. Still, Detroit possesses too much offensive firepower and trench dominance on Thanksgiving Day. Expect the Lions to pull away in the third quarter for a 31-17 victory, seizing sole possession of first place in the NFC North.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch, what to know and a prediction for the Thanksgiving clash between NFC East rivals Kathryn Riley / Getty Images FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys (5-6) have the chance to do something they haven't done yet in the 2026 season against the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) on Thanksgiving Day: win consecutive games. The only time the Cowboys have won back-to-back games under head coach Brian Schottenheimer came back in his first season in 2025 following their Week 10 bye. That was a stretch of three victories in a row against Las Vegas Raiders (33-16), the Eagles (24-21) and the Kansas City Chiefs (31-28) on Thanksgiving Day. After Dallas' 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans (1-9) on Sunday, Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones has some hope that his squad can make a postseason push down the stretch. That's just days after Jones called his Cowboys "a bad team" in the wake of their 46-40 home loss against the San Francisco 49ers (9-1) in Week 10. "It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we wanted to do," Jones said postgame on Sunday. "We needed this kind of thing. Any team does. We needed to feel it and get a little wind under our wings, so to speak." Quarterback Dak Prescott looks to continue his high-level play on Thanksgiving. If he replicated his Sunday performance against the Titans (325 yards passing and four touchdowns on 28-of-33 passing with a rushing touchdown), that would give Prescott 19 passing touchdowns on Thanksgiving, the record for the most Thanksgiving Day touchdowns in NFL history. Prescott's predecessor Tony Romo and Matthew Stafford currently share the record with 18 Turkey Day passing touchdowns each. "It's a blessing. It's something that, one of my favorite games of the year," Prescott said Tuesday. "And so, just being able to put that uniform on with the John Madden seal on it, understanding the whole world's watching and how many little kids are in the position that I once was: watching the game and then ready to go outside and play my own version of it. ... I don't take it for granted." However, there's one Cowboy who doesn't look forward to Thanksgiving: defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . The four-time Pro Bowler doesn't enjoy the holiday because it goes against his in-season training and diet regimen. Williams' go-to Thanksgiving side dish is macaroni, something that is hard to resist this time of year. "It's during the season. I'm trying to stay lean and trim, and it's a holiday right around when real football starts to come in," said Williams. "So I'm not a big fan of Thanksgiving." That's okay, because there will be plenty of fans ready to see Williams on the field, especially against starting Eagles quarterback and former Cowboy Joe Milton. Dallas acquired Milton in a trade with the New England Patriots in April 2025, and he worked as one of Prescott's backups until the Eagles signed him off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 17. That's the same day Philadelphia placed Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts (blood clots) on injured reserve. "Haha, it's good to see him," said Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb . "I hope he don't go crazy." Let's dig into the matchup. Where to watch Cowboys vs. Eagles live Date: Thursday, Nov. 26 | Time: 4:30 p.m. ET Location: AT&T Stadium (Arlington, Texas) TV: FOX | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Cowboys -8.5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Cowboys have the ball Prescott is cooking right now. He became the fourth player in NFL history with 300-plus passing yards and five-plus total touchdowns in consecutive games across Weeks 10 and 11, per CBS Sports Research. He joined Daunte Culpepper (2004), Tom Brady (2007) and Ben Roethlisberger (2014) in this exclusive club. After racking up 1,003 yards passing, 11 touchdowns and just a single interception over the last three weeks, Prescott now ranks second in the league in passing yards (3,049) and second in passing touchdowns (25). He also ranks eighth in touchdown-to-interception ratio (25-6) and passer rating (101.0) and fourth in expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.21) this season. Prescott credited his historic production to being able to play "balanced football" the last two weeks, with the Cowboys averaging the 12th-most rushing yards per game (125.5) since Week 10. "It really just opens up the whole playbook," Prescott said Thursday. "So it's a credit to all of it just, in that sense, coming together. Guys up front being physical in the run game, which then allows them to pass block a little bit easier there. And guys outside just getting open, making my job easier." In their 51-30 Week 11 win over the Titans, Schottenheimer provided Prescott and Co. their highest motion rate (63.5%) and play-action rate (58.3%) of the season, weeks after getting away from those staples through the first quarter of the year. Cowboys Pro Bowl wide receivers Lamb (1,108 receiving yards, the second most in the NFL) and George Pickens (780 receiving yards, the 11th most in the NFL) going up against the Eagles All-Pro cornerback tandem of Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean will be the key matchups on Thursday. However, Mitchell's status is uncertain due to a hamstring injury. The Eagles held walkthroughs on Monday and Tuesday, and they upgraded Mitchell to limited on Tuesday after he didn't participate on Monday. Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said Mitchell will be "fine" for Thanksgiving, and the Eagles listed him without a game status on the team's final injury report, indicating he will indeed play. When the Eagles have the ball When the Eagles have the football, they'll definitely be looking to play ground-and-pound football with 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Saquon Barkley . Barkley is currently on a streak of four consecutive games with a rushing touchdown, the longest streak of his career. The Cowboys have the worst run defense in football, allowing 151.5 rushing yards per game, and they struggle against Barkley's agile running style. Both Schottenheimer and Williams described Barkley as being a "jump cut" running back with how smoothly he can hit the hole and then glide to a different spot along the line of scrimmage and in the open field. Williams compared Barkley stylistically to Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving , who went off for 165 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in a 24-16 upset over the Cowboys in Week 5. Irving averaged a career-high 7.9 yards per carry that night at AT&T Stadium. Williams said the key is to stop Barkley's feet before he gets going. Williams also presents a challenge for Philadelphia as he leads the NFL with 18 tackles for loss, the most in a season by a defensive tackle since 2022. He also leads all defensive tackles in quarterback pressures (40) and co-leads his position in forced fumbles (4) along with Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter . Yet, he feels he can still find higher levels of play with the Cowboys defense allowing 20-plus points in 18 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the league. That's the longest such streak since the 2019-2021 Jacksonville Jaguars ' run of 25 straight games, per NFL Research . He completed 11 of his 21 throws for 141 passing yards while rushing for 7 yards on five carries. Prescott said he saw Milton develop most in Dallas on his mental side of the game and preparation as it pertains to pass protection adjustments and discernment at the line of scrimmage. "Joe is amazing, man. The athleticism that he has, the speed that he has, the arm talent that he has, he can do it all," Williams said. "So it's super dope to be able to go against him, especially after all the laughs and things we had in the locker room during training camp practices." The present iteration of the Eagles lacks the offensive artillery to win a duel with Prescott, Lamb and Pickens. That's especially true if Mitchell is unable to suit up on Thursday. Prescott is on a 20-game home winning streak against NFC East opponents, which is tied with Tom Brady (versus the AFC East) for the longest home winning streak by a starting quarterback against divisional opponents since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger. He'll break the tie with Brady with his 21st such victory in a row on Thanksgiving. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandon Lee Gowton · SB Nation Wed, November 25, 2026 at 5:34 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Philadelphia Eagles can avoid being some real turkeys by beating the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Fans would be very thankful to see a Birds win on Thursday. In order to preview this Week 12 NFC East battle, I reached out to our enemies over at Blogging The Boys . The divine Dave Halprin kindly took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let's take a look at the answers. 1 – To what extent do you buy Mike Pettine taking over play-calling making a positive difference for the Cowboys' defense? I'd say it somewhat made a positive impact. The defense against the Titans on Sunday certainly looked more coherent, especially in their coverage and with players being in proper position. There didn't seem to be so many busted assignments and guys not knowing what to do at the snap. There are reports they simplified the defensive calls and ran more zone coverage on the back end. The Titans did score three touchdowns, but one came on a questionable pass interference call in the endzone, another on a fluky run-after-catch where the Cowboys defender thought he touched the guy down but didn't, then a garbage time TD at the end of the game. So the 30 total points kind of seems larger than how it felt in the run of the game. Of course, having an offense score 51 points overwhelms all issues, but it still felt like a little bit better version of the Cowboys defense. 2 – Besides Christian Parker being demoted, what else has significantly changed for the Cowboys since they last played the Eagles? For one, the pass rush, While the Cowboys overall defense still struggles, in the four games since we last played the Eagles, Dallas has accumulated 17 sacks with plenty of other pressure that forces bad plays. Quinnen Williams has really taken his game up a notch and is terrorizing teams from the middle of the line. The defense still struggles against the run, and besides Joey Porter Jr. our cornerbacks can definitely be had on a regular basis. But the pass rush has become the one thing that really works on defense. On offense, it feels like Brian Schottneheimr has re-discovered motion, play-action, bunch sets, cutdown splits and other things that were severely under-used in the earlier part of the season. The Cowboys scored 40 points on a very good 49ers defense, and 51 points over the hapless Titans defense. The last two games have been more reminiscent of how good the offense had been previously rather than the inconsistent bunch we've seen at times in 2026. 3 – If the Cowboys lose to Joe Milton at home on Thanksgiving, would that be their most embarrassing possible loss this season? What's the path to the Cowboys losing this game? While it would be a bitter pill to swallow, we've already hit new lows by losing at home to a then-winless Buccaneers squad playing without Baker Mayfield, and allowed the terrible Cardinals to put together a comeback for the ages to win in Dallas. So losing to Joe Milton would make every fan gnash their teeth and then scream about not keeping him, but beating those other losses in the embarrassment category would be a hard thing to do. But, I won't count the Cowboys out, they just might find a way to out-embarrass themselves. The path to losing the game is kind of the same every week. The Cowboys defense plays horrible football, busting assignments, gathering penalties and basically making a joke out of form tackling. Then the offense goes into one of its inconsistent modes, where the play-calling is bad and penalties, drops or turnovers come home to roost. 4 – Which NFC East team is going to win this division? Who's going to finish second, third, and fourth? I was really leaning to the Cowboys because I just kept believing that the Giants would start to fall apart with their backup QBs playing. But that Jacksonville game where the Giants held on to victory makes me think that decent coaching (John Harbaugh) really can turn a team around. I'm still holding out hope we can catch them, but if I had to lay my life savings down on it, I'd have to take the Giants. As for the rest, it will probably end up the way it is now – Cowboys second, Commanders third and Eagles fourth. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Cowboys currently listed as 8.5-point home favorites, what's your score prediction? I'm taking the Cowboys because they are at home where the offense usually plays well, and the defense looks like it might just be getting incrementally better. The Eagles are trying to overcome a lot this season including injuries at QB and at other key positions. There just feels like a lot of turmoil over there and the Cowboys might be in the process of starting to play like we expected them to when the season began. I'll take the Cowboys 31-23.

Since Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen entered the NFL, the Chiefs and Bills have met four times in the playoffs. Allen and the Bills have lost all four times. Allen hasn't made a Super Bowl yet despite having a great career, and the biggest reason is Kansas City has stood in the way. The Chiefs had a stunning 6-11 record last season but have bounced right back. They're 8-2 to start this season. But the Bills are 9-1, and can practically knock one team out of its way in the race for the No. 1 seed by beating the Chiefs on Thursday. The big question for the Chiefs was if Kenneth Walker III could return from a groin injury, abut the Chiefs ruled him out on Wednesday. Rookie Emmett Johnson has played very well in his place, but Walker was one of the best backs in the NFL for the first half of the season. The Chiefs could miss him in a huge game. Johnson playing well is important because there could be bad weather. The forecast is for about 37 degrees with a 75% chance of rain at kickoff. There's also expected to be 19 mph winds, which could affect passing games. The Bills will be looking to ride Josh Allen for a big home win. With Allen, the Bills are 0-4 against the Chiefs in the playoffs, but 5-1 in the regular season against Kansas City. Another regular-season win over the Chiefs wouldn't ensure that they could knock off Kansas City in the postseason, if the two teams meet again, but it would likely mean that matchup would be in Buffalo. Patrick Mahomes of the Kansas City Chiefs and Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills have faced each other 10 times, including playoffs. Who needs it more? The Bills aren't getting endless shots at making a Super Bowl with Josh Allen. At some point this era will end, and it would be tremendously disappointing if it didn't include at least one trip to the final game. It's hard to think that far ahead, but this game is huge for the Bills in not only getting closer to the AFC's No. 1 seed but also making sure they won't be going to Kansas City in January. The Broncos, Jaguars and Bengals are all in the mix for the No. 1 seed, too, but the Chiefs have been such a problem for the Bills in the playoffs that it's OK to have a little more focus on being in a best position just in case they meet Kansas City again. The Chiefs don't want to fall two games behind the Bills and also lose ground on the Broncos in the AFC West, but this is a bigger game for Buffalo. Key player: Chiefs WR Josh Downs Downs has played just 28 snaps for the Chiefs since they acquired him in a trade with the Colts. But in those 28 snaps he has 10 targets, which is a great sign that Patrick Mahomes already trusts him and wants to get him involved. Downs has eight catches for 112 yards and a touchdown with Kansas City, which is tremendous efficiency for playing less than 25% of the offensive snaps in two games. The big question for this game will be if Downs is comfortable enough in the offense to take on at least half of the snaps in a huge game. Downs has already shown he can impact the Chiefs' offense, even without playing much. His role on Thursday will be a big story. Betting market watch Vikings-49ers was billed as the Game of the Year last Sunday; hopefully, Chiefs-Bills lives up to the hype. Buffalo has been good to bettors overall (8-2 against the spread) and at home (4-1 ATS), while Kansas City has lost both games outright and ATS on the road against potential playoff teams this season (20-3 at Seattle, 28-24 at Denver). Patrick Mahomes has also thrown for 942 yards and 10 TDs (with no INTs) in Kansas City's last three blowout wins against less competition (NY Jets, at Atlanta, Arizona). Buffalo has won six straight — including the last four by at least 17 points — but still seems a little under-discussed for a 9-1 football team. Mahomes is an impressive 13-4-1 ATS as an underdog in his career. My gut says Josh Allen finds a way to get this done. He saves his best for Mahomes, Andy Reid & Co. — and this is the regular season, where Allen has dominated this matchup. The Bills (-3) cover another classic between these two great QBs. — Ben Fawkes Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub . Here are three fantasy themes to track as you finish up the Thanksgiving slate. 1. Can Emmett Johnson do it again? The Chiefs wanted to get Kenneth Walker (groin) back after a two-game absence, but Emmett Johnson has been undeniably great as the temporary fill-in. Over the last two games he has 206 rushing yards and 108 receiving yards. He's in for another big workload on Thursday. 2. How much will Josh Allen run? Although Allen has continued to pile up the short-yardage touchdowns, his rushing production has been muted this year — he has just 51 rushing yards in the last five games, and he didn't have a single rushing attempt against Miami last week. The Chiefs have seen Allen plenty over the years, so they know how important it is to limit this element of his game. 3. What's the featured pitch in the Chiefs' passing game? Travis Kelce is coming off a two-score week, Josh Downs has hit the ground running with his new team, and Rashee Rice is a consistent factor on shorter routes. Patrick Mahomes is spreading the ball around, so it's hard to view any of these guys as an automatic fantasy start. But there's a plausible upside for all three, as well. — Scott Pianowski Check out more of Scott's work at the Yahoo Sports fantasy hub .
